question: Should OpenClaw add a plugin-visible skill install/update completion observer now, and what redacted payload and failure semantics should it expose?
rationale: The remaining gap is a new public plugin lifecycle/security contract, not a missing implementation detail; maintainers need to choose how much install outcome data plugins may observe and whether observer failures can affect installation.

options.title: Add a minimal non-blocking observer
options.body: Expose redacted target/provenance/outcome/timestamp metadata after skill install/update completion, log observer failures, and keep blocking decisions in `security.installPolicy` and `before_install`.

options.title: Defer to operator policy only
options.body: Close the post-install observer gap as not planned and direct security tooling to pre-install policy plus diagnostic audit instead.

options.title: Broaden lifecycle hooks
options.body: Fold this into a larger skill lifecycle API covering install, update, uninstall, and execution hooks, accepting a slower product/API design cycle.

recommendation.title: Add a minimal non-blocking observer
recommendation.body: Expose redacted target/provenance/outcome/timestamp metadata after skill install/update completion, log observer failures, and keep blocking decisions in `security.installPolicy` and `before_install`.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision extends the install-policy/security boundary that this owner most recently implemented and proved across skill and plugin install paths.
